Chapter 7. Navigating Setbacks and Loss with Intention.
Life’s storms—nobody gets a free pass, do they? Loss, disappointment, those sudden setbacks—they’re just part of being human. But here’s something worth holding onto: when we bring intention into the picture, even our toughest moments can become unexpected sources of strength and wisdom.
Picture this. Someone loses a job they really loved. The shock hits hard—suddenly, fear, anger, and self-doubt all come crashing in. For days, even getting out of bed feels impossible. Every mistake plays on repeat in their mind. But then, maybe while sitting in the quiet, they remember something about intention. And instead of the usual, “Why did this happen to me?” a new question pops up—“What is life inviting me to learn or become?”
That shift doesn’t wipe away the pain. But it cracks open a little doorway. They quietly set an intention—to stay resilient, to keep an open heart—even though uncertainty still hangs in the air. Then, little signs of support start to show up: a friend calls just to check in, maybe a new opportunity appears out of nowhere, and before long, hope starts to peek through the clouds. Months later, looking back, it’s clear—the setback wasn’t the end of their story. It was actually a turning point.
Grief works the same way. Imagine someone mourning a loved one, feeling lost in waves of sadness. By setting an intention—to honor their feelings and stay open to healing—they begin to notice gentle moments of peace, even while grieving. A memory sparks a smile, a quiet walk in nature brings a bit of comfort, and slowly, life starts to feel possible again.
Most of us try to dodge pain, thinking maybe if we just stay positive, we’ll keep trouble away. But intention doesn’t mean pretending everything’s fine or slapping a happy face on hard times. It’s really about showing up for each moment—whether it’s joyful or painful—with presence and a sense of purpose. It’s trusting that, even in the darkest times, there’s a deeper current moving us forward.
And here’s the thing: over time, setbacks lose some of their power to scare us. They’re still tough, but we stop seeing them as failures or punishments. Instead, we start to understand—they’re just part of the journey. They’re invitations to grow, to let go, and to discover strengths we never knew we had.
So, intention becomes our steady companion. It’s there, guiding us, no matter what life throws our way—helping us navigate both the rough patches and the moments of joy, one step at a time.
